description_full: IBEX Limited provides end-to-end technology-enabled customer lifecycle experience solutions in the United States and internationally. The company's products and services portfolio includes ibex Connect that offers customer service, technical support, revenue generation, and other value-added outsourced back-office services through the CX model, which integrates voice, email, chat, SMS, social media, and other communication applications; ibex Digital, a customer acquisition solution that comprises digital marketing, e-commerce technology, and platform solutions; and Wave iX, an AI customer experience platform. It operates customer engagement and customer acquisition delivery centers. The company serves government, banking and financial services, delivery and logistics, health tech and wellness, high tech, retail and e-commerce, streaming and entertainment, travel and hospitality, and utility industries. IBEX Limited was formerly known as IBEX Holdings Limited and changed its name to IBEX Limited in September 2019. The company was incorporated in 2017 and is headquartered in Washington, District Of Columbia.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 35K people. Revenue per employee of $18K ranks in the bottom quartile among Technology peers, improving at 7%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $891 of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $221 per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 94× revenue per employee (high relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (5/10).
financial_summary: IBEX Limited is a small-cap technology business with a $661M market cap on $644M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 33% against a 9% cost of capital — a 24-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $31M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.27× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 59× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 3.9% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

Trading near 52-week highs — the market has already recognised the story

Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sect: Its 9% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.36x its revenue share).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-15.9% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 17% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 1% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 36% and a beta of 0.85, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.39 vs 5y 0.74), so read it loosely.
About $4.3M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 46% in the 2020 crash and 22% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 50% below its DCF fair value of $98.13, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 11%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $56.28 to $173 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 15.8 vs 26.7 and EV/EBITDA 7.3 vs 16.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 4.7% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 9.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 2 covering analysts target $42.00 on average, 15% below the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 3.0% annual cash-flow growth, 12pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 33% clears the cost of capital of 9.0% by 24pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.05).
It converts 5% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.27x.
ROE of 27% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
It spends 1.2% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $30.9M (5% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 7.2% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 77% of profits supports about 25.7% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.4x, 4.3% of sales), a maintenance pace.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 10.0% on average.
Analysts expect 10.4% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.9%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (7 sales, net $1.9M sold).
It returns 2.2% a year to shareholders (2.2% in buybacks).
people: With about 35,000 employees, each generates about $18K of revenue, 0.0x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 7.2% a year.
CEO pay is $1.7M (94x revenue per employee).
